name: POST /api/mcp/tools/:tool_id/invoke — invoke a registered MCP tool under a capability token

testCases.name: 400 - a tool_id that is not a UUID is refused before it reaches the query
400 - a well-formed tool_id with an incomplete body names what is missing

description: Invokes a registered MCP tool. RETARGETED: this definition previously pointed at POST /mcp/v1/call with a {name, arguments} body — a route and a contract that do not exist on the gateway, so it could only ever 404. The real surface is /api/mcp/tools/:tool_id/invoke, gated by requireAuth, taking {agent_run_id, capability_token_id, args, trace_id}. The cases below cover the two validation contracts the handler states explicitly and which need no producer chain: a tool_id that is not a UUID is refused with 400 rather than being allowed to reach the UUID query and surface as a Postgres 22P02 500, and a well-formed tool_id with an incomplete body is refused with 400 naming the missing fields. The happy path additionally requires a live agent run and a minted capability token, so it is left to the integration suite rather than asserted here with fabricated ids.

errorCases.name: 400 - malformed tool_id
errorCases.message: tool_id must be a valid UUID
errorCases.when: the path carries a literal placeholder or any non-UUID; refused deliberately so it cannot reach the UUID query and 500 as Postgres 22P02

errorCases.name: 400 - missing required invocation fields
errorCases.message: agent_run_id, capability_token_id, args and trace_id are required
errorCases.when: any of the four required body fields is absent — an invocation without a capability token is exactly what the gate exists to refuse

errorCases.name: 401 - missing bearer token
errorCases.when: the route is behind requireAuth, so an unauthenticated invoke never reaches the handler
